audit_scope.description: Prague fork transaction validation exceptions, EIP-4938 eth/67 wire protocol migration, Cancun block environment opcodes, EIP-3651 warm COINBASE, and EIP-4895 beacon chain withdrawal processing

in_scope: Transaction type validation and exception handling (Prague)
Block environment opcodes (BLOCKHASH, COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, NUMBER, PREVRANDAO, GASLIMIT, CHAINID)
EIP-2929 access list initialization with warm COINBASE (EIP-3651)
Withdrawal balance application and withdrawals_root validation (EIP-4895)
out_of_scope: Init code size limits (internal validation only)

misclassified_entities.reason: This is an internal EL component that iterates through withdrawals in the execution payload. It is not an external entity crossing a trust boundary; it is part of the block processing pipeline within the EL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC / P2P Mempool
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transactions arrive from unauthenticated external users via public JSON-RPC endpoints or P2P gossip. The submitter identity is verified only by ECDSA signature on the transaction itself, but the transaction content (type, fees, authorization lists) is untrusted and must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer via devp2p Wire Protocol (eth/67)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers communicate over unauthenticated P2P connections. Any peer can send arbitrary wire protocol messages including deprecated message types. Messages must be validated for type, format, and content before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer via Snap Sync Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Snap protocol peers provide state data (trie nodes, bytecodes) over unauthenticated P2P connections. Responses must be verified against known state roots to ensure correctness, as peers may serve malicious or incorrect data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (Validator) via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers submit execution payloads containing block headers and withdrawal data via the Engine API, which is authenticated with JWT. However, the proposer controls block parameters (coinbase, timestamp) within protocol bounds and the payload content must still be validated (e.g., withdrawals_root verification).

trusted_external_entities.name: CL via Engine API (PREVRANDAO Provider)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (prev_randao field in payload attributes)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The consensus layer provides the PREVRANDAO value through the authenticated Engine API. The value is derived from beacon chain randomness which individual validators can influence to a limited degree. The channel is JWT-authenticated but the randomness quality depends on honest validator majority.

trusted_external_entities.name: CL via Engine API (Withdrawal Provider)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (withdrawals field in execution payload)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The consensus layer provides validated withdrawal lists to the EL via the JWT-authenticated Engine API. The CL has already validated withdrawal parameters and assigned monotonic indices. However, the EL must still verify the withdrawals_root commitment matches the provided data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain Validator (Withdrawal Initiator)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon chain voluntary exit / withdrawal credential
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators initiate withdrawals through the beacon chain protocol. Their identity is cryptographically authenticated via BLS signatures, but withdrawal parameters pass through CL validation before reaching the EL. The validator is semi-trusted because they are authenticated but could attempt to manipulate withdrawal amounts or addresses.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All transaction fields must be validated: type byte must be recognized (0-4), fee structure must satisfy maxFeePerGas >= baseFee and maxPriorityFeePerGas <= maxFeePerGas, blob transactions must have valid versioned hashes and non-empty blob data, and EIP-7702 authorization lists must be non-empty.

Message type codes must be validated against the eth/67 supported set. Deprecated message types (0x0d GetNodeData, 0x0e NodeData) must be rejected. Malformed or oversized messages must not cause resource exhaustion.

All snap protocol responses (ByteCodes, TrieNodes) must be verified against known state roots. Peers may provide incorrect or incomplete data. Response sizes must be bounded to prevent memory exhaustion.

Execution payload must be validated: withdrawals_root must match computed Merkle-Patricia trie root of withdrawal list. Block timestamp and coinbase are proposer-controlled but must be within protocol bounds.
PREVRANDAO value is accepted as-is from the authenticated Engine API channel. Contracts should not rely on it for high-value randomness as it can be influenced by validators.

Withdrawal list integrity must be verified via withdrawals_root. Withdrawal amounts are in Gwei and must be correctly converted to Wei. Balance updates are unconditional and must not fail. The bounded quantity of withdrawals per block must be enforced.
Validator withdrawal requests must be authenticated via BLS signatures. Withdrawal indices must be monotonically increasing and never duplicated to prevent replay attacks.
